changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from CV Intoxicating Substances Reference: the shared sympathomimetic toxidrome plus per-agent distinguishing features and management for cocaine, amphetamine/dextroamphetamine, methamphetamine, MDMA/MDA, synthetic cathinones, methylphenidate, and caffeine.

summary: One shared sympathomimetic toxidrome — tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, mydriasis, diaphoresis, agitation — with benzodiazepines and active cooling as the common core of management. What differs by agent: cocaine's sodium-channel cardiotoxicity, methamphetamine's long half-life, MDMA's paired hyperthermia-and-hyponatremia, the cathinones' immunoassay-negative agitated psychosis, and caffeine (the one where beta-blockade is not a trap).
whyThisMatters: Stimulant toxicity is a large and rising share of ED and prehospital agitation, hyperthermia, and chest pain, and the mistakes are agent-specific: giving an unopposed beta-blocker in cocaine toxicity, over- or under-hydrating an MDMA patient without checking the sodium, discharging a methamphetamine patient expecting a cocaine-length course, or anchoring on a negative tox screen in a floridly psychotic young patient who took a synthetic cathinone the assay cannot see.
clinicalTakeaway: Treat the shared adrenergic driver first: benzodiazepines titrated to effect for agitation, hypertension, tachycardia, and seizure prophylaxis, plus active external cooling for hyperthermia (antipyretics do not work). Then apply the agent-specific move — sodium bicarbonate for a wide QRS (cocaine, high-dose stimulants); check serum sodium in any altered or seizing MDMA patient; treat suspected synthetic-cathinone psychosis on clinical grounds with benzodiazepine + antipsychotic; and remember caffeine tachydysrhythmia takes esmolol, not the cocaine 'avoid beta-blockade' rule. Aggressive fluids and early cooling prevent the rhabdomyolysis-DIC-AKI cascade rather than treating it after the fact.

body.text: Stimulants raise synaptic monoamine tone (dopamine, norepinephrine, ± serotonin) and produce a common picture: tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, mydriasis, diaphoresis, and agitation. Route, transporter pharmacology, and the co-released neurotransmitter burden determine which complications dominate. Common management core: benzodiazepines first-line (addresses the shared adrenergic driver — agitation, hypertension, tachycardia, seizure prophylaxis), active external cooling for hyperthermia (treat as excited-delirium physiology, not infectious fever — antipyretics are not indicated), and aggressive IV fluids with early cooling to pre-empt rhabdomyolysis, DIC, and AKI. Refractory agitation / excited delirium → ketamine with airway readiness, then dexmedetomidine for ICU maintenance. Wide QRS or ventricular dysrhythmia → sodium bicarbonate; avoid lidocaine and class Ia/Ic antiarrhythmics.

columns: Management specifics beyond the shared core
rows: Cocaine

Class Ic-like sodium-channel blocker — wide-complex dysrhythmia mimics TCA overdose, pro-convulsant. Coronary vasospasm; treat chest pain as possible ACS. Levamisole adulterant (up to 70-80% of US supply): retiform purpura of ears/cheeks/nose + neutropenia + dual p-/c-ANCA = essentially diagnostic. Half-life ~1 h; benzoylecgonine on UDS 2-4 days

Bicarbonate for wide QRS. Nitroglycerin / calcium-channel blocker for vasospasm; aspirin. AVOID unopposed beta-blockade acutely — if rate control needed, labetalol per AHA/ACC after benzodiazepines + vasodilator. Consider aortic dissection / cardiomyopathy for cocaine chest pain once ACS excluded
Amphetamine / dextroamphetamine

Transporter-reversal releaser. No exam finding distinguishes it from methamphetamine — the clue is context (prescribed ADHD med, crushed/insufflated tablet, adolescent diversion). Half-life 10-13 h, pH-dependent renal elimination
Supportive, benzodiazepine-centered; no specific antidote. Activated charcoal if early after a large protected-airway oral ingestion. Bicarbonate if QRS widening
Methamphetamine

More lipophilic, longer half-life (6-15 h, commonly 11-12) than cocaine — agitation and psychosis are prolonged and resource-intensive. Chronic stigmata: "meth mouth" (cementoenamel-junction caries, blackened crumbling teeth, xerostomia, bruxism) + formication excoriations on face/forearms/legs

Benzodiazepine doses often higher (tolerance). Active cooling, IV fluids for rhabdomyolysis risk. Plan disposition/staffing for an 8-hour course, not a cocaine-length one. Whole-bowel irrigation can be considered for body packers
MDMA / MDA

Potent serotonin releaser + ADH release → free-water retention. The two dominant killers are hyperthermia and hyponatremia, not cardiac events. Near-universal bruxism/trismus. Hyperthermia + hyponatremia together is distinctive; inducible clonus confirms serotonin toxicity

Check serum sodium in any altered or seizing MDMA patient BEFORE deciding on fluids. Hyponatremic seizure → 100 mL 3% saline, correct ≤ 6-8 mEq/L/24 h. Ice-water immersion for T > 40 °C; dantrolene has case support > 40-42 °C. Cyproheptadine for benzo-refractory serotonin features
Synthetic cathinones ("bath salts", MDPV, mephedrone, alpha-PVP/flakka)

Structurally heterogeneous — no single toxidrome; skewed toward severe, prolonged agitated psychosis out of proportion to cardiovascular findings. Routine immunoassays do NOT detect them — a negative screen in a floridly psychotic young patient raises suspicion, not lowers it

Treat the syndrome, not a lab. Benzodiazepines + antipsychotic (e.g. olanzapine) titrated aggressively. Aggressive cooling; IV fluids for rhabdo-associated AKI. Low threshold to admit; plan early for airway if sedation requirements climb
Methylphenidate

Pure reuptake inhibitor — overdose is clinically indistinguishable from amphetamine. Crushed ER tablet can dump a full day's dose; OROS "ghost tablet" can appear intact in stool (normal PK, not unabsorbed drug). IV/insufflation misuse → filler microembolization
Supportive, benzodiazepine-centered, mirrors amphetamine. Charcoal for large recent oral ingestion. Embolic phenomena or multi-organ dysfunction from IV misuse → ICU workup
Caffeine

Adenosine A1/A2A antagonist (+ PDE inhibition, catecholamine release at toxic dose). Marked hypokalemia out of proportion to GI losses (catecholamine-driven intracellular shift — over-correction risks rebound hyperkalemia). Lethal serum level ~80-100 μg/mL; LD50 ~150-200 mg/kg (~10-14 g). 1 tsp powder ≈ 2,700 mg

Esmolol is first-line for tachydysrhythmia — beta-blockade is NOT a trap here (no unopposed-alpha problem). IV fluids, correct hypokalemia carefully, benzodiazepines for seizures. Supralethal ingestion → lipid emulsion + hemodialysis (case reports); early nephrology/tox consult. Psych eval before discharge for intentional overdose

body.text: Believe a positive cocaine UDS (benzoylecgonine has essentially no cross-reactant) but do not anchor on it — the route of use predicts the complication, so always ask how the patient uses. Conversely, a negative standard screen does not exclude synthetic cathinones or many designer stimulants. Once acute intoxication resolves, do not reflexively withhold a guideline-indicated beta-blocker (HFrEF, prior MI) on the basis of remote cocaine history alone.
